subject: Unexpected 429s: cap-override, evidence handoff, and credit offer for Mosaic Health
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mosaichealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@mosaichealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T08:12:00Z
Subject: High spike of 429s this morning — urgent

Hi Jordan,

We started seeing a spike of 429s across our tenant at ~07:45 PT and it looks correlated to a batch job from our claims-enrichment pipeline. The errors began causing downstream retries and slowed a critical SLA job for our ops team. Attached is a short snippet of the client logs from our side and a few request IDs.

Can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (rate limits, quotas, routing)? This is impacting our on-call rotation and we need an ETA for recovery.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Torres
SRE, Mosaic Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T08:34:00Z
Subject: Re: High spike of 429s this morning — urgent

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the log snippets, they were helpful. We're treating this as high priority. Initial summary: we see a quota-namespace mapping mismatch for Mosaic Health's tenant alias that caused per-tenant enforcement to pick the wrong cap window when a burst job hit. That resulted in unexpected 429 responses between ~07:44 and 09:00 PT.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Opened an emergency cap override for Mosaic Health at 08:28 PT to prevent further user-facing 429s (this bypasses enforcement for 2 hours while we investigate).
- Fingerprinted the failing request IDs you sent and pulled server-side traces.
- Notified Engineering on call to run a configuration rollback if required.

Short answers to your questions:
- No planned config changes were deployed this morning. The issue appears to be a config translation bug that surfaced during a recent alias migration.
- ETA for full remediation: we expect to complete the root-cause fix and revert the override by 15:30 PT today, with a postmortem and evidence packet delivered by end of day.

I'll follow up with a clear timeline and a proposed credit for the impact window. Apologies for the disruption — we know how disruptive retries like this can be.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T09:02:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Mosaic Health — quota-namespace mapping mismatch, emergency override active

Team — quick sync notes so customer-facing comms are aligned. Summary: Mosaic's tenant alias (mosaic-prod / tenant-id 0x9b3a) ended up pointing at the legacy quota namespace during the alias migration last week. The legacy namespace has a hard burst window of 120k tokens/min which is much lower than their expected dedicated cap, so a burst job tripped enforcement and returned 429s.

What we did:
- Cap override engaged at 08:28 PT (temporary bypass).
- Rolled forward a safe translation change at 09:10 PT that re-mapped the alias to the correct namespace in the config store; the override will be revoked once we validate no regression in the next 30 minutes.
- Exported request traces and KV cache snapshots (attached to this thread).

Customer impact window: 07:44–08:28 PT (customer saw errors until we applied the override) and a residual 08:28–09:10 PT where the override reduced 429s substantially.

Proposed remediation to offer the customer (please review/comments):
- One-time usage credit worth the estimated extra cost and retries for the primary impact window (proposal: 10% of June invoice or $12,000 token-credit, whichever is higher).
- Deliver full evidence package (server traces, enforcement logs, configuration diffs) by EOD.
- Postmortem draft + improvements: add alias-migration validation in CI, automated QA check for quota-namespace consistency, and an admin alert to detect anchoring to legacy namespaces.

Ben: can you prepare a warm credit proposal and the comms for procurement?
Aditya: can you validate the config diffs and confirm whether any other tenants share the same migration path?
Evelyn: please coordinate the postmortem and compliance-friendly evidence bundle.

Thanks — Jordan
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@mosaichealth.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@mosaichealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T15:48:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: remediation summary, evidence, and credit offer (Mosaic Health)

Hi Alex / Sanjay — thanks again for your patience today. Below is a concise summary of what happened, what we did, and next steps. We will attach the full evidence bundle (server traces, enforcement logs, and config diffs) in the folder linked in this email and copy the SOC/Procurement friendly files for your records.

What happened
- Root cause: alias migration produced a mapping inconsistency that left Mosaic Health tied to a legacy quota namespace with a lower burst window; when your claims-enrichment batch ran, enforcement returned 429s.
- Impact window: 07:44–08:28 PT (user-facing errors); residual elevated rejection rate until 09:10 PT while we validated the remap.

What we did
- Emergency cap override at 08:28 PT to reduce user-facing 429s immediately.
- Corrective config remap at 09:10 PT and validation run completed at 09:35 PT.
- Delivered live traces and enforcement logs to your SRE (attached).

Customer remediation offered
- Credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit equal to $12,000 (token-credit) against June charges to compensate for retries and operational impact. If you prefer a percentage credit instead, we can apply 10% of the invoice — let us know which is easier for your finance team.
- Evidence: attached bundle ("postmortem-draft-mosaic-20260629.md") plus raw logs (mosaic_health_qos_logs_20260629.zip).
- Postmortem: draft is attached and we will finalize after a short review with your SREs.

Follow-ups / next steps
- Ben will send the formal credit note to Procurement and initiate the internal billing workflow for the credit (expected completion 2026-07-02).
- Evelyn will share the finalized postmortem and a short remediation roadmap to prevent recurrence (changes to alias migration CI + automated namespace-consistency check).
- Jordan / Engineering will run a scan for other tenants that used the same migration path and produce a report by 2026-07-01.

Attached: mosaic_health_qos_logs_20260629.zip; redwood_credit_proposal_mosaic_8792.pdf; postmortem-draft-mosaic-20260629.md

Apologies again for the disruption — we appreciate the quick reports from your team which helped us remediate faster. Please let us know if you want the credit processed as a balance adjustment or a pro-forma invoice reversal.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

--
Ben Carter (on billing) will follow up separately about the credit paperwork.
